Most mornings I lose 30–40 minutes standing in front of the bathroom mirror, leaning in, turning my head different angles, comparing old photos, zooming in on my nose and eyes on my phone. Other days, if I’m already feeling panicky about it, I’ll avoid mirrors completely and walk around my apartment half in the dark so I don’t have to see my face.

The anxiety is constant but very focused on this: how my face looks, whether people are judging me, whether cameras or bright lights will make the flaws obvious. I’m not up at night worrying about money or my job performance in general—just this one thing, over and over.
